Semen: prostate. Semen, also known as seminal fluid, is a bodily fluid that contains spermatozoa from the male gonads of animals.
In which country is Thalidomide scandal?
Thalidomide scandal: Germany. It was introduced as a sedative and medication for morning sickness without having been tested on pregnant women.
Who is credited with discovering Flerovium?
Flerovium: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Flerovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Fl and atomic number 114.
Who is credited with discovering Hypochlorous acid?
Hypochlorous acid: Antoine Jérôme Balard. Hypochlorous acid is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula ClOH, also written as HClO, HOCl, or ClHO.
Who is credited with discovering Gallium?
Gallium: Paul-Émile Lecoq de Boisbaudran. Gallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ga and atomic number 31.
Heading Switzerland's Federal Department of Home Affairs for over a decade, this politician succeeded Marija Pejčinović Burić atop a major European institution in 2024 — who is he?
Alain Berset (French; born 9 April 1972) is a Swiss politician who served as a Member of the Swiss Federal Council from 2012 to 2023.
With a wingspan up to 3.3 meters and a weight of 15 kilograms, which South American bird is generally considered the largest bird of prey on Earth, sporting a ruff of white feathers around its neck?
Andean condor (Vultur gryphus) is a South American New World vulture and is the only extant member of the genus Vultur.
Excavated in Argentina starting in 1989 under paleontologist José Bonaparte, this Late Cretaceous titanosaur weighed as much as 80 tons — which genus of giant sauropod?
Argentinosaurus (meaning "lizard from Argentina") is a genus of giant sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period in what is now Argentina.

Manufactured by a Turkish company and credited largely to a former MIT graduate, this medium-altitude combat drone has become one of the most exported unmanned aircraft of its era — what aircraft (family) is it?
Baykar Bayraktar TB2 is a family of medium-altitude long-endurance (MALE) unmanned combat aerial vehicles (UCAV) capable of remotely controlled or autonomous flight operations.
A child prodigy who wrote a treatise on conic sections at 16, which Frenchman later traded letters with Fermat on probability and built early calculating machines?
Blaise Pascal (19 June 1623 - 19 August 1662) was a French mathematician, physicist, inventor, philosopher, and Catholic writer.
This small leafy vegetable, a cultivar of cabbage grown for its edible buds, shares its name with a European capital — what is it?
Brussels sprout is a member of the Gemmifera cultivar group of cabbages (Brassica oleracea), grown for its edible buds.

This American astronomer and planetary scientist was initially an assistant professor at Harvard before moving to Cornell as the David Duncan Professor of Astronomy. He played an active role in the Voyager programs. Who is he?
Carl Sagan (November 9, 1934 - December 20, 1996) was an American astronomer, planetary scientist and science communicator.

Once prized as refrigerants and aerosol propellants — Freon being the famous example — these halogenated compounds were phased out under the Montreal Protocol for gnawing holes in the ozone layer — what are they?
Chlorofluorocarbon (CFCs) and hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFCs) are fully or partly halogenated hydrocarbons that contain carbon (C), hydrogen (H), chlorine (Cl), and fluorine (F).
In mathematics, this term describes a selection of items from a set in which the order of choosing doesn't matter — unlike its counterpart, the permutation. Name the concept?
Combination is a selection of items from a set that has distinct members, such that the order of selection does not matter (unlike permutations).
A creeping vine of the gourd family that originated across Asia from India to Yunnan, this annual comes in slicing, pickling, and seedless types — what is it?
Cucumber (Cucumis sativus) is a widely-cultivated creeping vine plant in the family Cucurbitaceae that bears cylindrical to spherical fruits, used as culinary vegetables.

Lean, fast, and wedge-skulled, this medium-sized Australian canine comes in ginger, black-and-tan, or creamy white, and scientists still argue whether it's a dog, a wolf subspecies, or its own species — what is it?
Dingo is a lineage of dog found in Australia.

This scientific and engineering discipline uses transistors, diodes, and integrated circuits to control and amplify the flow of electric current, converting between forms like AC to DC. What is the field called?

Electronics is a scientific and engineering discipline that studies and applies the principles of physics to design, create, and operate devices that manipulate electrons and other electrically charged particles.
This U.S. Marine turned professor wrote a 1981 memoir of his WWII combat, later adapted into a Ken Burns documentary and an HBO miniseries where he was played by Joseph Mazzello — who was he?
Eugene Sledge (November 4, 1923 - March 3, 2001) was a United States Marine, university professor, and author.

This region of the upper limb, running between the elbow and the wrist, contains two long bones, the radius and the ulna, and is technically distinct from the 'arm' proper in anatomy — what is it called?
Forearm is the region of the upper limb between the elbow and the wrist. It is homologous to the region of the leg that lies between the knee and the ankle joints, the crus.
Among the longest of all living crocodilians, this fish-eater has a slender snout lined with 110 interlocking teeth and a pot-shaped bulb on the males' noses — what is it?
Gharial (Gavialis gangeticus), also known as gavial or fish-eating crocodile, is a crocodilian in the family Gavialidae and among the longest of all living crocodilians.
A retrovirus that gradually dismantles the human immune system, it leads to AIDS and, untreated, shortens life by roughly a decade — what is it?
HIV (HIVs) are two species of Lentivirus (a subgroup of retrovirus) that infect humans.
First unearthed in 1994 in Spain's Gran Dolina cave, this Early Pleistocene human was named 'pioneer man' because it was among the first to settle Western Europe. Which species is it?

Homo antecessor (Latin for 'pioneer man') is an extinct species of archaic human recorded in the Spanish Sierra de Atapuerca, a productive archaeological site, from 1.2 to 0.8 million years ago during the Early Pleistocene.
Aided by Soviet intelligence gathered on the American Manhattan Project, this physicist oversaw the first Soviet nuclear weapon test at Semipalatinsk in 1949 — who is he?
Igor Kurchatov was Soviet nuclear physicist (1903–1960).
Trained in biochemistry and physiology before ranging into geography and anthropology, this American author won the 1998 Pulitzer for Guns, Germs, and Steel — who is he?
Jared Diamond (born September 10, 1937) is an American scientist, historian, and author.
Born in 1972, this Canadian atmospheric scientist holds an endowed public-policy chair at Texas Tech and in 2021 became Chief Scientist at the Nature Conservancy — who is she?
Katharine Hayhoe (born 1972) is a Canadian atmospheric scientist.
Named for the German city where it was bred in the mid-19th century, this is a large German dog breed — which breed?
Leonberger is a German breed of large dog. The breed name derives from that of the city of Leonberg, in Baden-Württemberg, where it was bred in the mid-nineteenth century.
Reclassified in 2021 as part of the order Psocodea alongside booklice and barklice, these tiny wingless parasites cement their eggs to a single host for life — what are they called?
Louse (pl.: lice) is the common name for any member of the infraorder Phthiraptera, which contains nearly 5,000 species of wingless parasitic insects.
Google's employee No. 20 and its first woman software engineer, she later left to run a famous internet company as CEO from 2012 until Verizon bought it — who is she?
Marissa Mayer (born May 30, 1975) is an American business executive, software engineer, and investor who served as president and chief executive officer of Yahoo!
Connecting the diencephalon and cerebrum to the pons, this brainstem structure plays a role in vision, hearing, and staying alert -- what is it called?
Midbrain is the uppermost portion of the brainstem connecting the diencephalon and cerebrum with the pons.
This semiaquatic rodent can stay submerged for up to seventeen minutes, propelled mainly by its webbed hind feet while its long, scaly tail helps steer — what animal is it?
Muskrat (Ondatra zibethicus) is a medium-sized semiaquatic rodent.
First isolated by Scottish physician Daniel Rutherford, which group-15 nonmetal with atomic number 7 is the most abundant species in Earth's atmosphere?
Nitrogen is a chemical element; it has symbol N and atomic number 7.
This systemic skeletal disorder develops when the rate of bone breakdown outpaces new bone formation with age, leaving bones porous, less dense, and prone to fracture — what's the condition called?
Osteoporosis is a systemic skeletal disorder characterized by low bone mass, micro-architectural deterioration of bone tissue leading to more porous bone, and consequent increase in fracture risk.
Brought on by too little niacin, this disease announces itself with the 'three D's' — dermatitis on sun-exposed skin, diarrhea, and dementia — what is it?
Pellagra is a disease caused by a lack of the vitamin niacin (vitamin B3).
Which condition, more common in people with obesity or a family history, involves hair and skin debris being drawn into tissue through tiny skin openings called pits?
Pilonidal disease is a type of skin infection that typically occurs as a cyst between the cheeks of the buttocks and often at the upper end.

Native to North American grasslands, these burrowing, herbivorous ground squirrels come in five species, black-tailed, white-tailed, Gunnison's, Utah, and Mexican. Name this genus, Cynomys, by its common two-word name?
Prairie dog (genus Cynomys) are herbivorous burrowing ground squirrels native to the grasslands of North America.

This small herbivore belongs to the family Leporidae alongside hares, and the European species of its genus has been introduced to every continent except Antarctica — what bouncy little prey animal is it?
Rabbit are small mammals in the family Leporidae (which also includes the hares), which is in the order Lagomorpha (which also includes pikas).

Nicknamed 'Il Professore' for his academic background, this Italian politician served as European Commission President from 1999 to 2004 and was twice his country's prime minister, first after leading The Olive Tree coalition to victory — who is he?

Romano Prodi (born 9 August 1939) is an Italian politician who served as President of the European Commission from 1999 to 2004 and twice as Prime Minister of Italy, from 1996 to 1998, and again from 2006 to 2008.
Developed by the MIT Media Lab for children ages 5 to 16, this block-based visual programming language and website has been translated into more than 70 languages — name it?
Scratch (programming language) is a high-level, block-based visual programming language and website aimed primarily at children as an educational tool, with a target audience of ages 5 to 16.
Famous for their slowness, these tree-dwelling Neotropical mammals are closest relatives of anteaters and come in just seven living species across two genera — what are they?
Sloth are a Neotropical group of xenarthran mammals constituting the suborder Folivora, including the extant arboreal tree sloths and extinct terrestrial ground sloths.
Director of research at Cambridge's Centre for Theoretical Cosmology, he was the Lucasian Professor of Mathematics from 1979 to 2009. Who?

Stephen Hawking (8 January 1942 - 14 March 2018) was an English theoretical astrophysicist, cosmologist, and author who was director of research at the Centre for Theoretical Cosmology at the University of Cambridge.
One of the oldest constellations, this zodiac figure once marked the Sun's place at the spring equinox and inspired bull imagery from Sumer to Rome — which northern-sky constellation is it?
Taurus (constellation) (Latin, 'Bull') is one of the constellations of the zodiac and is located in the northern celestial hemisphere.
Joining Bethesda Game Studios in 1994, this video game director has since led development of both The Elder Scrolls and Fallout series, as well as 2023's Starfield. Who is he?
Todd Howard (born 1970) is an American video game designer, director, and producer who serves as director and executive producer at Bethesda Game Studios.
Native to cool climates across the Northern Hemisphere, this low shrub bears small, round, edible fruit of a deep blue color, and goes by several folk names depending on region — what's the species?
Vaccinium myrtillus is a holarctic species of shrub with edible fruit of blue color, known by the common names bilberry, blaeberry, and whortleberry.
The first person to ever call himself a psychologist, this German founder of modern psychology launched Philosophische Studien, the field's first academic research journal — who is he?
Wilhelm Wundt (16 August 1832 - 31 August 1920) was a German physiologist, philosopher, professor, and one of the fathers of modern psychology.

This symptom can stem from something as mild as gastroenteritis or as serious as a ruptured aortic aneurysm or ectopic pregnancy, yet its exact cause goes unexplained in about a third of cases — what symptom is this?
Native to China and Taiwan, this fast-growing deciduous tree can reach 15 meters in 25 years and has become notorious in North America as a host plant for the invasive spotted lanternfly. What is it?
Ailanthus altissima: Deciduous tree in the quassia family.
Prized for its oil since Spanish and Portuguese traders carried it from South America to Europe in the 1600s, this citrus-scented herb also goes by 'beebrush' — what's its species name?
Aloysia citrodora: Species of plant. Aloysia citrodora, lemon verbena, is a species of flowering plant in the verbena family Verbenaceae, native to South America.
A towering 20th-century French mathematician known for foundational work in number theory and algebraic geometry, he was a principal founder of the Bourbaki group. Who was he?

Named from a Tupi word imitating the sound these macaws make, this genus of large, vividly colored Neotropical parrots includes eight living species prized — and poached — for the pet trade — which genus?
Ara (bird): Neotropical genus of macaws. Ara is a Neotropical genus of macaws with eight extant species and at least two extinct species.
This ocean giant, recorded at up to 680 kg, has vanished from the Black Sea but still roams the Mediterranean and both sides of another major ocean — which fish?
Atlantic bluefin tuna: Species of fish. The Atlantic bluefin tuna (Thunnus thynnus) is a species of tuna in the family Scombridae.
Bred in Britain to hunt rabbits and hares, this scent hound's keen nose also makes it a popular detection dog for smuggled food at airports — which breed?
Beagle: Breed of small scent hound. The Beagle is a British breed of scent hound, similar in appearance to the much larger foxhound.
Colloquially called a buffalo in the US and Canada, this large bovine is actually more closely related to yaks and cattle than to true buffalo — which animal?
This white crystalline sodium borate dissolves in water to form a basic solution and finds uses as a pesticide, a soldering flux, and an ingredient in glass and pottery glazes — what mineral is it?
Borax: Boron compound, a salt of boric acid.
This condition involves inflamed, fluid-filled sacs that normally cushion friction near joints like the shoulder, elbow, hip and knee — what is it?
Bursitis: Inflammation of the bursae (sacs of synovial fluid in joints)
Native to the Americas, this plant genus in the nightshade family produces the fruits we call peppers, including sweet bell types and fiery chilies — what genus is it?
This bacterial skin infection affects the dermis and subcutaneous fat, most often striking the legs or face and causing spreading redness and swelling — what is it?
Cellulitis: Bacterial infection of the inner layers of the skin called the dermis.

A yellowish-green gas that turns reddish-brown liquid when cooled and bright orange crystals when colder still, this compound is usually handled in solution and used as a bleach and disinfectant — what is it?
Native to the Americas from Mexico to South America, this diurnal member of the Procyonidae family goes by the name 'quash' in Belize — what is it?

Known to NATO by the reporting name 'Mop' and to Canadian forces as the Canso, this WWII flying boat served every branch of the U.S. military and remained in some air forces into the 1980s — which aircraft?
Consolidated PBY Catalina: American 1930s flying boat.
Native to the Andes and Mesoamerica, this plant genus includes five edible species known variously as squash, pumpkin or gourd — which genus?
Native to Madagascar and grown ornamentally throughout the tropics, this legume tree is known for its fern-like leaves and a flamboyant summer display of orange-red blossoms — what is it?
Delonix regia: Species of flowering plant in the bean family Fabaceae.
Also nicknamed the French Mastiff, this large, powerfully muscled brachycephalic breed ranks among France's heaviest dogs — which breed?
Dogue de Bordeaux: Dog breed originating in France.

A British physicist who hauled a captured German thermionic valve back from the Western Front, he won the 1947 Nobel for mapping the ionosphere — work that paved the way for radar and shortwave radio. Who was he?

Native across the arctic and temperate Northern Hemisphere, this fern relative grows both a spore-bearing stem and a separate sterile green one, and is often mistaken for mare's tail — what plant is it?
The only member of its family found outside the Americas, this tiny insect-eating bird holds its short tail erect and is unusually polygynous for a songbird — what is it?
Eurasian wren: Species of bird. In Anglophone Europe, it is commonly known simply as the wren.
Born Leonardo Bonacci in Pisa, this medieval Italian mathematician's 1202 book 'Liber Abaci' introduced Europe to Indo-Arabic numerals and a famous number sequence bearing his nickname — who is he?
Dubbed the "Flying Tailor," this inventor was so sure his wearable parachute would work that he leapt from the Eiffel Tower to test it himself — fatally. Who was he?
With a siphon that can stretch over three feet and a shell just 6 to 8 inches across, this giant Pacific burrowing clam can live up to 179 years — which creature?
Caused by the bacterium Neisseria gonorrhoeae and colloquially called 'the clap,' this sexually transmitted infection can pass from mother to child during birth — what is it?
Gonorrhea: Sexually transmitted infection. Gonorrhea or gonorrhoea, colloquially known as the clap, is a sexually transmitted infection (STI) caused by the bacterium Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
This North Atlantic member of the true cod family is prized smoked as Finnan haddie or the Arbroath smokie — what fish is it?
Haddock: Species of fish. The haddock (Melanogrammus aeglefinus) is a saltwater ray-finned fish from the family Gadidae, the true cods.
This inflammation of the liver can cause jaundice and, if it becomes chronic, progress to cirrhosis — most commonly caused by five different viruses labeled A through E. What condition is it?
Hepatitis: Inflammation of the liver. Hepatitis is acute if it resolves within six months, and chronic if it lasts longer than six months.
The most widespread of all primates, this bipedal, nearly hairless species owes its advanced technology, culture, and language to a large, complex brain — what is it?
Human: Species of hominid in the genus Homo.
Typically starting to work within an hour, this NSAID relieves pain, fever, and inflammation but can worsen asthma and, in later pregnancy, is considered harmful — which drug?

Credited with the oldest known systematic classification of chemical substances, this alchemist's corpus also contains the earliest instructions for deriving ammonium chloride from organic matter — who is he?
Jabir ibn Hayyan: Islamic alchemist and polymath (died c. 806–816)
Building his first firearm at age 13 in his father's gun shop, this American designer earned 128 patents and pioneered the autoloading pistol — who is he?
In this eye disorder, the cornea gradually thins and bulges into a cone shape, causing blurry or double vision often linked to excessive eye rubbing as a risk factor — which condition?
Keratoconus: Medical condition involving the eye.
At Bologna in the 1700s she became the first woman to hold a science doctorate and the first salaried female university teacher — depicted as the goddess Minerva herself; who was she?
Laura Bassi: Italian physicist and academic (1711–1778)
This soft, movable pair of appendages on the jaw helps with eating and speech, and is often used in kissing — what are they?
Lip: Visible body parts at the mouth.
Named from the Latin for "wolf," this autoimmune disease often announces itself with a red facial rash and alternates between flares and remission — what is it?
Lupus: Autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks healthy tissue.
Boiled down from its sap to make a beloved breakfast syrup, this genus of roughly 132 tree and shrub species counts the sycamore as its type species — which genus of trees?

Fever, a fierce headache, neck stiffness, and a telltale rash that doesn't fade when a glass is rolled over it can signal this inflammation of the membranes around the brain and spinal cord — what is it?

Meningitis: Inflammation of membranes around the brain. Meningitis (pl. meningitides) is acute or chronic inflammation of the protective membranes covering the brain and spinal cord, collectively called the meninges.

NATO called it 'Farmer,' and this Soviet twin-engine fighter was the first Soviet production aircraft capable of supersonic speed in level flight, later battling American jets over North Vietnam — which aircraft?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-19: Air superiority fighter aircraft family.
Native to northern India, this fast-growing, drought-resistant tree is nicknamed the 'drumstick tree' for its seed pods and the 'horseradish tree' for its pungent roots — what is it?
Moringa oleifera: Species of flowering tree.
Sold as Aleve, this NSAID eases pain, fever, and menstrual cramps for up to twelve hours, and also comes in a more soluble sodium form — which drug?
Naproxen: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) used to treat pain.

Usually made from unleavened dough that's rolled, cut, or extruded into long strips, this staple food is called pasta in Italian cuisine and split into wheat-based and starch-based varieties in Chinese cooking — what is it?
Noodle: Staple food made from unleavened dough, commonly long and thin.

Born out of military planning before World War II, this branch of applied mathematics uses optimization and statistics to find the best possible outcome for real-world decisions — what field, sometimes called management science?
Operations research: Discipline concerning the application of advanced analytical methods.
Also called the corn poppy or Flanders poppy, this red flowering weed has symbolized remembrance in the Commonwealth since World War I — what plant is it?
Papaver rhoeas: Species of flowering plant in the poppy family.

This term for 'parts in each thousand' is symbolized by ‰ — a percent sign with an extra zero — and sits right next to the percent sign in Unicode's General Punctuation block — what is this unit called?
Per mille: Unit for parts per thousand. The associated symbol is ‰, similar to a per cent sign % but with an extra zero in the divisor.

For two thousand years it lived inside natural philosophy alongside chemistry and biology, only breaking off as its own discipline during the 17th-century Scientific Revolution; what is this study of matter, energy, and force?
Physics: Scientific field of study. It is one of the most fundamental scientific disciplines.
First domesticated some 5,000 years ago on the Iranian plateau, this fruit-bearing shrub reached California in 1769 via Spanish settlers — which fruit?
Pomegranate: Fruit-bearing deciduous shrub. Pomegranate was first domesticated by ancient Iranians in the Iranian plateau and nearby regions about 5,000 years ago.
Created in the early 18th century, this dark pigment was the first modern synthetic color, made by oxidizing iron ferrocyanide salts — what is it?
Prussian blue: Synthetic pigment. Prussian blue (also known as Berlin blue, Brandenburg blue, Parisian and Paris blue) is a dark blue pigment produced by oxidation of ferrous ferrocyanide salts.
Element 88 reacts with nitrogen rather than oxygen in air, turning black, and once glowed in self-luminous paints despite being highly carcinogenic — which element is it?
Radium: Chemical element with atomic number 88 (Ra)
Curving around the chest, these bones protect the lungs and heart and, in snakes, support and protect the whole body — what are they called?
Rib: Long bone in vertebrates that protects vital respiratory and cardiovascular organs.
First identified in Wuhan in late 2019 and once provisionally called 2019-nCoV, this positive-sense RNA virus is the one that causes COVID-19 — what's its official name?
SARS-CoV-2: Virus that causes COVID-19. The virus previously had the provisional name 2019 novel coronavirus (2019-nCoV), and has also been called human coronavirus 2019 (HCoV-19 or hCoV-19).
After early family-friendly Christian games found little success, which developer switched to horror in 2014 and created a hit franchise of horror video games?
Scott Cawthon: American video game developer (born 1978)
Named for a Swedish medical physicist, this SI unit measures the stochastic health risk of ionizing radiation, such as equivalent and effective dose — what unit is it?
Sievert: Derived SI unit of equivalent dose of ionizing radiation. One sievert equals 100 rem, which is an older, CGS radiation unit.
Native to the tropical Americas and a cousin of the cherimoya, which spiny fruit smells like pineapple and tastes like strawberries and apple with a sour citrus tang?
Soursop: Tropical fruit tree. Soursop (also called graviola, guyabano, and in Hispanic America guanábana) is the fruit of Annona muricata, a broadleaf, flowering, evergreen tree.
A member of the rose family, this bright red treat is botanically not a berry at all, and each of its 'seeds' on the outside is really a tiny fruit called an achene — what is it?
Strawberry: Edible fruit. The garden strawberry (or simply strawberry; Fragaria × ananassa) is a widely grown hybrid plant cultivated worldwide for its fruit.

This mammal family includes true digging specialists as well as aquatic desmans and the water-and-tunnel-adept star-nosed species, absent from Ireland but found from Eurasia to as far south as tropical Southeast Asian mountains — which family?
Talpidae: Family of small insectivorous mammals.

Comprising two Einstein-authored physics frameworks published in 1905 and 1915 — one covering phenomena without gravity, the other explaining gravitation itself — this pair introduced four-dimensional spacetime and superseded Newtonian mechanics. Which pair of physics frameworks is this?
Theory of relativity: Two interrelated physics theories by Albert Einstein.
This central part of the body, from which the head, neck, limbs, and tail extend, is divided into chest, abdomen, and pelvic segments — which body part?

Torso: Central part of the living body. The tetrapod torso — including that of a human — can be divided into segments:

The chest or upper torso.

A reddish-purple natural dye secreted by sea snails in the Muricidae family, also called royal purple or imperial dye. The colored compound is 6,6'-dibromoindigo, extracted from snails like Bolinus brandaris. What is this ancient dye?
Tyrian purple: Natural dye extracted from Murex sea snails. The name Tyrian refers to the city of Tyre in ancient Phoenicia (modern-day Lebanon).
Native to southwestern Europe, this venomous viper is also called the asp or aspic viper, with about 4% of untreated bites proving fatal — which snake?
Vipera aspis: Species of snake. Its common names include asp, asp viper, European asp, and aspic viper, among others.

By measuring weak natural radioactivity with sensitive Geiger counters, this American chemist developed a dating method in 1949 that revolutionized archaeology — and won him a 1960 Nobel Prize. Who was he?
Known on the street as a date-rape drug but used medically to treat narcolepsy and cataplexy, this natural neurotransmitter is also a precursor to GABA in the brain — what compound is it?

Γ-Hydroxybutyric acid: Chemical compound. γ-Hydroxybutyric acid, also known as gamma-hydroxybutyric acid, GHB, or 4-hydroxybutanoic acid, is a naturally occurring neurotransmitter and a depressant drug.
Berkelium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for berkelium is Bk. Berkelium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Bk and atomic number 97.
